We recently announced a new, dedicated hub in the Gemini app to help get students started with all of Gemini's learning tools. Initially available in personal accounts, the Gemini student hub is now available to Google Workspace for Education users of all ages. The hub helps keep students organized; they can start a study notebook, create flashcards, take a practice quiz, and more. As Gemini creates more learning tools, you’ll find them in the student hub.

Getting started


Admins: The Gemini app and related in-app tools are controlled by the Generative AI settings in the Workspace Admin console. The Gemini student hub is subject to these existing controls. Visit the Help Center for more information on turning the Gemini app on or off.
End users: There is no end user setting for this feature. To get started, visit gemini.google.com/students or select Students in the Gemini app menu.


Rollout pace


Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains: Available now


Availability


Available to all Google Workspace customers and Workspace Individual subscribers outside of the European Economic Area (EEA), and users with personal Google accounts globally


Resources


News from Google: Start the semester with one year of Gemini, on us

We recently introduced skills—reusable prompts that guide Gemini—in the Gemini app and Google Workspace. Over the coming weeks, skills will roll out to Workspace users and eventually replace Gems as the tool for tailoring instructions for specific tasks.

Read on for more details on skills, plus critical information and dates related to the transition away from Gems in the Gemini app, Workspace, Google Classroom, and more.
What are skills?
Skills are reusable, custom instructions that you can leverage any time you’re prompting Gemini in the Gemini app and most Workspace apps. For example, you can create a brand voice skill to help you draft blog posts or a lesson planning skill to save time with class prep. You can even use multiple skills in the same prompt or at different points in the conversation.


To learn more about skills and how to create them in the Gemini app, Gemini Enterprise, and Workspace, business and enterprise users should check out our AI skills 101 handbook. Educational institutions should leverage our Gems transition guide for education. For a comprehensive list of resources, see the bottom of this post.


Note: Currently, skills do not sync between the Gemini app and Workspace apps. If you want to use a skill across both platforms, you must create it separately in each.

# How to Use Gemini's New Student Hub and Skills for Studying

> **In short:** Google says it has rolled out a dedicated student hub inside the Gemini app and a new "skills" feature that lets you save reusable instructions. The student hub is open to Google Workspace for Education users and personal account holders globally (outside the EEA), and the skills rollout is happening in waves.

If you've ever sat down to study and spent more time figuring out *how* to use your AI helper than actually learning, Google's latest Gemini changes are aimed squarely at you. Two separate updates, both with a learning flavor, just landed — and together they make Gemini more useful for homework, class prep, and self-study. Here's what's new, and how to actually find each feature.

## What the student hub is

The Gemini student hub is a single place inside the Gemini app that gathers Google's learning tools. According to Google, students can use it to:

- Start a **study notebook**
- Create **flashcards**
- Take a **practice quiz**
- Access any new learning tools Google adds in the future

Think of it as a front door. Instead of hunting through the menu every time you want to quiz yourself, you go to one spot and everything study-related is right there.

## What "skills" are

Skills are reusable instructions — short, saved prompts (a prompt is just the text you type to an AI) — that you can apply to any conversation with Gemini. Google gives two examples in its announcement:

- A **brand voice skill** that helps you draft blog posts in a consistent tone
- A **lesson planning skill** that helps speed up class prep

You can use more than one skill in the same chat, or layer them in at different points. According to Google, skills are rolling out to Workspace users over the coming weeks, and they will eventually replace **Gems** — the older feature that did something similar.

One small gotcha Google flags: skills do not currently sync between the Gemini app and Workspace apps. If you want the same skill in both places, you have to create it twice.

## How to open the student hub

Before you start, a quick check: the student hub is available to **personal Google account holders globally** and to **Google Workspace for Education users of all ages** — but it is **not** available in the European Economic Area (EEA). If you are in the EEA, this part of the guide won't apply to you yet.

1. **Go to the student hub directly.** Open `gemini.google.com/students` in your browser. You will land inside the hub, where the study notebook, flashcards, and practice quiz tools live.
2. **Or find it in the Gemini app menu.** Open Gemini, look at the menu (the list of options inside the app), and select **Students**. The same set of tools will appear.
3. **Sign in with the right account.** If you use both a personal Google account and a school Workspace account, make sure you're signed in to the one you want to study with before you open the hub.

If you're a Workspace admin, the Gemini app and the student hub are controlled by the **Generative AI settings** in the Workspace Admin console — so if your students can't see it, that's the first place to check.

## How to try a skill

Skills are still rolling out, so what you see may depend on your account. Here's the general flow, based on how Google describes it:

1. **Open the Gemini app** (or a supported Workspace app like Google Docs).
2. **Look for the skills option** in the prompt area — Google has been adding a skills entry point where you normally type your prompt.
3. **Pick a built-in skill to start with.** Rather than writing one from scratch, browse what Google offers. A "lesson planning" skill, for example, would shape every response to fit that task.
4. **Try it on a real task.** Type a prompt the skill is meant for and send it. You'll know the skill is working when the response follows the structure or tone the skill is built around — for instance, a lesson plan skill should return a formatted plan rather than a generic essay.
5. **Stack a second skill if it helps.** If you also have a "concise" skill, you can apply it on top, in the same chat, to tighten up the output.

## A few practical use cases

- **Quiz yourself before a test.** Open the student hub, start a practice quiz on the topic you're revising, then save a "study coach" skill that asks you to explain your wrong answers back in your own words.
- **Speed up class prep.** If you teach, a lesson planning skill turns a one-line prompt ("plan a 45-minute lesson on photosynthesis for 6th graders") into a structured outline — every time, without retyping the same instructions.
- **Keep your voice consistent.** A brand voice skill (or a "personal writing" version) helps you write essays, blog drafts, or emails in the same style, so you don't have to think about tone.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a student**: start with the student hub. It's the lowest-effort way to try Gemini's learning tools — the flashcards and practice quiz are the most directly useful for exam season.
- **If you're a teacher or tutor**: the lesson planning skill is the time-saver to try first. One saved prompt, reused every week, adds up fast.
- **If you use Gems already**: heads up — Google says skills will eventually replace Gems. Worth experimenting with skills now so the transition is smooth later.
- **If you already use Gemini for studying**: create one skill for the task you do most often (summarizing notes, making flashcards, drafting essay outlines) and reuse it instead of re-explaining yourself each time.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Expecting the student hub to appear in the EEA.** It isn't there yet, according to Google's rollout note.
- **Creating the same skill twice on purpose.** Right now skills don't sync between the Gemini app and Workspace apps, so if you only need it in one place, make it there.
- **Writing long, complicated skill prompts.** Skills work best when the instruction is short and specific — "always end with three quiz questions" beats "be a helpful study assistant who does many things."
- **Forgetting which account you're signed into.** The student hub and skills behave differently across personal, Workspace, and Workspace for Education accounts.

## Wrap-up

Two updates, one direction: Google is tidying up how people learn with Gemini. The student hub puts the study tools in one place, and skills let you save the instructions you keep retyping. Pick one — the hub if you're a student, skills if you teach or write — and spend ten minutes this week trying it. That's all the setup it takes to know whether it earns a permanent spot in your study routine.
